metaDescription: Six Bluetooth trackers compared for iPhone and Android, with notes on battery type, ring volume and wallet or key fit, so you can pick the right tag.
introParagraphs: Losing keys, a wallet or a bag for ten minutes is annoying, and a Bluetooth tracker turns that hunt into a button press. The tag rings when it is close and, when it is far away, shows its last known spot on a map using other people's phones. Choosing one is mostly about matching the tag to your phone and to the thing you keep misplacing.

We evaluated six current trackers based on product specs and buyer feedback, looking at which network each one uses, how the battery works, how loud the ring is and what shape the tag takes. Two of them work on either Apple Find My or Google Find Hub, one is built around Tile's own app for any phone, one is Apple's own AirTag, one is a thin wallet card and one is an iPhone-only tag with a swappable coin cell.
Read the compatibility notes first, because a tag locked to the wrong network is the most common regret, then use the tables to settle on a battery style and pack size.

products.name: Chipolo POP Tracker Tag, Find My or Find Hub

specList.label: Networks
specList.value: Apple Find My or Google Find Hub

products.description:
The Chipolo POP is the most balanced tag here because it covers both phone worlds and rings very loudly. At setup you choose Apple Find My or the Google Find Hub network, and the listing says the ring reaches up to 120 dB. A keyring hole is molded in, so no extra holder is needed to put it on house or car keys.

The bright casing is a real advantage for anyone who drops keys on a dark carpet, since you can spot it as well as hear it. The tradeoff is that a single tag can only live on one network at a time, so a household that mixes iPhone and Android cannot share one tag between phones. The listing also does not state a battery type or water rating, so we do not claim either.

Ownership is simple: pair it, clip it on and ring it from the app. Chipolo backs it with a 2-year warranty and says replacements go through the seller on Amazon. Next to the Apple AirTag it publishes a clear decibel figure where Apple gives only a 50% louder speaker, though the AirTag has precision finding that the POP lacks, and next to the Chipolo CARD it suits keys rather than a wallet.
products.bestFor: Anyone who wants one loud, bright key tag that works on iPhone or Android.
pros: Listing quotes a ring of up to 120 dB for hunting under cushions
You can choose Apple Find My or Google Find Hub when you set it up
A keyring hole is built in, so no separate holder is required
Bright colors make the tag easy to spot on a dark floor as well
cons: One tag sits on one network, so it cannot serve both phone types
Listing gives no battery type, so replacement plans are unclear
No precision direction finding like the AirTag offers on iPhone

products.name: Apple AirTag (2nd Generation)
specs: Apple Find My, iPhone and iPad
products.description:
The second generation AirTag is the pick for iPhone owners who want the tightest integration. It sets up with one tap on an iPhone or iPad and lives in the Find My app. Precision Finding gives step by step directions to a lost item, and it now works on Apple Watch too, while upgraded Ultra Wideband and Bluetooth chips extend how far away you can ping it.

Apple also describes a speaker that is 50% louder with a new chime, and a sharing option that lets you give temporary location access to trusted contacts, third parties or over 50 airline partners. That airline feature is handy for checked luggage. The big tradeoff is platform lock: it only works with Apple devices, so an Android phone cannot use it at all.

There is no keyring hole on the bare tag, so most people add a holder to put it on keys. The listing is sold as a single and as a 4-pack. Compared with the Chipolo POP at up to 120 dB it relies on the chime plus precision arrows rather than raw volume, and against the Ultrbeka 4-pack with IP67 it gives you far deeper iPhone features.
products.bestFor: iPhone and Apple Watch owners who want arrow-guided finding and luggage sharing.
pros: Precision Finding points the way on iPhone and now Apple Watch
The speaker is 50% louder with a new chime that is easier to know
Share a location with trusted people or over 50 airline partners
One tap setup with an iPhone or iPad inside the Find My app today
cons: Apple devices only, so Android phones cannot use this tag at all
Bare tag has no keyring hole, so a holder is needed for keys
The listing gives no battery type or water rating to compare it

products.name: UGREEN Finder Duo Air Tracker Tags 4 Pack

specList.label: Networks
specList.value: Apple Find My or Google Find Hub

products.description:
The UGREEN Finder Duo is the multi-pack for people who dislike buying coin cells. Each tag charges over a universal USB-C port and the listing says a charge lasts 365 days. It pairs with an iPhone through Apple Find My or an Android phone through the Google Find Hub app, and the listing says it is certified by both Apple and Google.

Alerts are covered too: the app can warn you when a tag moves out of range with a last known location, and Lost Mode lets you leave contact details for a finder. Privacy is described as end-to-end encrypted. The tradeoff is the rechargeable design, since you need a charging cable and a reminder once a year, and a sealed cell is harder to swap than a coin battery.

Four tags cover keys, a bag, a backpack and a pet or luggage tag in one box. Next to the Ultrbeka 4-pack, which uses a replaceable CR2032, the Duo trades easy battery swaps for USB-C top ups, and compared with the Chipolo POP it gives you four tags rather than one but no stated dB figure.
products.bestFor: Households that want four tags on either network and prefer charging to coin cells.
pros: USB-C charging means no disposable batteries to buy for the tags
Listing states 365 days of battery from a single full charge
Certified for Apple Find My and Google Find Hub in one product
Lost Mode lets a finder see your contact details if it is found
cons: You must remember to recharge each tag about once every year
Sealed rechargeable cell cannot be swapped like a coin battery
The listing gives no ring volume or water rating to compare it

products.name: Chipolo CARD Rechargeable Wallet Tracker

specList.label: Networks
specList.value: Apple Find My or Google Find Hub

products.description:
The Chipolo CARD is built to ride in a wallet, passport pouch or ID holder rather than hang from a keychain. It is thin enough to slide in with your cards, and like the POP it works with Apple Find My or Google Find Hub, so Android owners are covered. You ring it from the app to find a wallet hidden nearby, or look it up on the map when it is further away.

The battery is rechargeable through a Qi magnetic wireless charger and lasts up to a year on a charge. The listing states the charger is not included, which is the main gotcha, because you need to supply one. Chipolo also gives a 2-year warranty and free replacement through the Amazon seller if something goes wrong.

It makes sense as a second tag alongside a keychain model. At up to 1 year per charge it matches the UGREEN Finder Duo's 365 days, but it is one flat card instead of four tags, and next to the Chipolo POP it gives up the keyring hole and the 120 dB figure for a slimmer body. The listing gives no loudness or water rating for the card itself.
products.bestFor: People who lose a wallet or travel documents more than they lose keys.
pros: Thin card shape slides into a wallet or passport pouch easily
Works with both the Apple Find My and Google Find Hub networks
Rechargeable battery lasts up to a year on a single full charge
Two-year warranty with free replacement through the Amazon seller
cons: The Qi magnetic charger is not included, so you must supply one
No keyring hole, so it is not the right tag for a bunch of keys
The listing gives no ring volume or water rating for the card

products.badge: Best Replaceable Battery Pack for iPhone
products.name: Ultrbeka Air Tag Tracker 4 Pack, MFi Certified
products.description:
The Ultrbeka 4-pack is a plain, practical tag for iPhone owners who want a swappable battery and a stated water rating. It uses Apple Find My and is MFi certified, plays a sound through the app to help find nearby items, and relies on Apple devices passing by to update the location when it is far away. The listing is clear that it is a Find My accessory, not an AirTag.

Durability is the headline: an IP67 rating protects against dust and water, and each tag takes a replaceable CR2032 coin cell so you never throw a tag out for a flat battery. The tradeoff is that it only supports iPhone and iPad, and the listing gives no ring volume or precision finding. It will not suit anyone on Android.

Four tags go on keys, a handbag, a backpack and luggage or a bike. Against the UGREEN Finder Duo, which is rechargeable and works on both networks, the Ultrbeka is the better choice if you would rather buy a coin cell than charge a tag every 365 days, and compared with the Apple AirTag it offers the IP67 figure that the Apple listing does not state.
products.bestFor: iPhone owners who want four rugged tags with batteries they can swap themselves.
pros: IP67 rating protects tags from dust and water on daily carry
A replaceable CR2032 battery keeps each tag going for many years
MFi certified for Apple Find My with sound played from the app
Four tags cover keys, bags, luggage and a bike in a single pack
cons: Apple devices only, so Android phones cannot use any of these tags
The listing gives no ring volume figure or precision finding
The coin cell must be bought and swapped by hand over the years

products.name: Life360 Tile Bluetooth Tracker, iOS and Android
products.description:
The Tile is the odd one out because it runs on its own network and app rather than Find My or Find Hub. That makes it the easiest answer for a family that mixes iPhone and Android, since one free app works on both. You can ring the tag, follow it on a map, or press it to make your phone ring, even when the phone is silenced.

There are two extras that the other tags here lack. A discreet SOS alert can notify your loved ones if you feel unsafe, and the tags can be added to the Life360 family safety app so everything shows on one map. The tradeoff is that you depend on the Tile network, and the listing gives no battery type, water rating or loudness figure.

It is sold as a single, a 2-pack or a 4-pack and attaches to keys, bags or a water bottle. Compared with the Chipolo POP at up to 120 dB it is a quieter promise on paper, and against the AirTag it trades Apple's precision finding for support on every phone, which is why it works as a single gift tag for a mixed household.
products.bestFor: Mixed iPhone and Android families who want one app and a safety alert.
pros: One free app works for both iPhone and Android users at home
Press the tag to ring your phone, even when the phone is silenced
Discreet SOS alert can notify loved ones in an unsafe moment
Sold as 1, 2 or 4 packs so you can buy only what you really need
cons: Runs on the Tile network, not Apple Find My or Google Find Hub
The listing gives no battery, water rating or loudness figure
SOS and map extras only help if family members use Life360 too

buyingCriteria.explanation: Compatibility decides whether a tag works at all. Apple Find My tags need an iPhone or iPad, Google Find Hub tags need Android, and a single tag only joins one network at a time. The Apple AirTag and Ultrbeka 4-pack are iPhone only, while the Chipolo POP, Chipolo CARD and UGREEN Finder Duo let you pick Find My or Find Hub at setup. Only the Life360 Tile runs the same app on both phone types, so mixed households should start there.

Trackers use either a swappable coin cell or a rechargeable cell, and each has a chore attached. The Ultrbeka uses a replaceable CR2032, the UGREEN Finder Duo lasts 365 days per USB-C charge, and the Chipolo CARD runs up to 1 year on a Qi magnetic charge with the charger sold separately. A coin cell suits people who dislike cables, while rechargeable suits people who dislike buying batteries. Set a yearly reminder either way.

A tag you cannot hear under a couch cushion is only half useful. The Chipolo POP lists up to 120 dB, which is the loudest figure in this group, and the AirTag has a speaker 50% louder than before with a more distinctive chime. Listings for the Tile and Ultrbeka give no decibel figure, so judge those by buyer feedback. If you are hard of hearing in high pitches, favor the louder tags.

A round keychain tag is wrong for a wallet, and a card is wrong for a keyring. The Chipolo CARD is thin enough for a wallet or passport pouch, while the Chipolo POP has a keyring hole molded in. The bare AirTag has no hole, so budget for a holder if it will live on keys. Match shape to the item you lose most, then buy extras for the rest.

Bluetooth only reaches a short distance, and beyond that the network of passing phones does the work. Find My uses Apple devices, Find Hub uses Android devices, and Tile uses its own network. The UGREEN Finder Duo adds out of range alerts and Lost Mode, and the AirTag adds sharing with over 50 airline partners for luggage. Remember that a tracker shows a last known location, not live GPS.

Keys and bags get rained on, so a stated rating beats a vague claim. The Ultrbeka lists IP67, which covers dust and brief immersion, while the Chipolo POP and CARD list a 2-year warranty with free replacement through the seller. Several listings, including the Tile and AirTag, state no water rating. If a tag will ride in a coat pocket in all weather, favor a published rating or a warranty.

howWeEvaluated.title: Network and phone support
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked which phones and networks each tag supports, since a tag on the wrong network is useless. The Chipolo POP, Chipolo CARD and UGREEN Finder Duo cover Find My and Find Hub, the AirTag and Ultrbeka are Apple only, and the Tile runs its own app on every phone. Clear, stated compatibility earned the most weight.

howWeEvaluated.title: Battery design
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared battery type and stated life as the listings describe them. The UGREEN Finder Duo claims 365 days per charge, the Chipolo CARD claims up to 1 year, and the Ultrbeka uses a replaceable CR2032. Where a listing was silent, as with the Tile and AirTag, we did not assume a figure.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ring volume and finding tools
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at how each tag helps you find it nearby. The Chipolo POP states up to 120 dB, the AirTag adds Precision Finding on iPhone and Apple Watch, and the Tile can ring your phone from the tag. All numbers are manufacturer claims, so we treated them as relative and balanced them against buyer feedback.

howWeEvaluated.title: Form and durability
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered whether the shape suits the job and how well it resists weather. The Chipolo CARD is wallet thin, the Chipolo POP has a built-in keyring hole, and the Ultrbeka lists IP67. A stated rating or warranty counted for more than a general claim of toughness.

howWeEvaluated.title: Lineup positioning
howWeEvaluated.description: We placed each pick by what it does best in this group, not by price. The Chipolo POP leads on stated loudness, the AirTag on iPhone integration, the UGREEN Finder Duo on rechargeable multi-pack value, the Chipolo CARD on wallet fit, the Ultrbeka on IP67 with swappable batteries and the Tile on cross-phone simplicity. We did not rank on popularity or review counts.

faq.q: Which Bluetooth tracker is best for most people?
faq.a: For most households, the Chipolo POP is the safest all-round choice because it works on Apple Find My or Google Find Hub and lists a ring of up to 120 dB. iPhone and Apple Watch owners may prefer the AirTag for Precision Finding. A mixed-phone family should consider the Life360 Tile.

faq.q: Can one tag work with iPhone and Android together?
faq.a: Not on the Apple and Google networks. A Chipolo or UGREEN tag lets you choose Find My or Find Hub at setup, but one tag joins only one network at a time. The Tile is the exception because its own app runs on both phone types.

faq.q: Do I need a subscription for a tracker?
faq.a: The Find My tags in this list, including the AirTag and Ultrbeka, use Apple's network without a separate monthly plan stated in the listing. The other listings we reviewed do not describe a subscription either. Check the app for any optional premium features before buying.

faq.q: Is a Bluetooth tracker the same as a GPS tracker?
faq.a: No, and this is the most common misconception. These tags use Bluetooth to ring nearby and depend on passing phones to report where they last were. If no compatible phone walks by, the location can be old. They are for keys, wallets and bags, not live tracking.

faq.q: How often do I need to change or charge the battery?
faq.a: It depends on the design. The UGREEN Finder Duo lists 365 days per USB-C charge, the Chipolo CARD lists up to 1 year per charge, and the Ultrbeka uses a replaceable CR2032. Set a yearly reminder, and test the ring each time you swap or charge a tag.

faq.q: Can a tag be used to track me without my knowing?
faq.a: Certified trackers are designed so phones warn you about unknown tags traveling with you, as a privacy safeguard. If you see an unknown tracker alert, follow the prompts on your phone. Never place a tag on another person or their property without their consent.

faq.q: Should I put a wallet tracker and a key tag on the same network?
faq.a: Yes, that is usually simpler. Keeping every tag on one network means one app and one set of alerts. The Chipolo POP and Chipolo CARD both support Find My and Find Hub, so you can match them to your phone and manage them together.
